content:
**brain:ticket:start resolves its base from the epic's declared tracker**

A slice no longer starts from main because nobody remembered --base. parseTicketArgs gains baseExplicit (the default 'main' stays, so 'nobody asked' and 'the caller asked for main' are finally different facts) and offTracker. The decision itself moved into a pure leaf, lib/ticket-base.mjs: resolveBase reads the issue's parent, then that node's tracker, honoured only when the node declares kind: epic — one hop, with the issue reader injected so every row is tested without a repository or a forge. It never returns main silently: no parent, a parent that is not an epic, an epic with no tracker and an epic that cannot be read each carry their own stated reason, and the unreadable case FAILS OPEN because a forge outage must not stop every session that starts a slice (the rule already written at ticket-start.mjs:151-154). One refusal only: an explicit --base main against a declared tracker, naming the tracker, the epic and --off-tracker. The leaf returns message keys, never rendered text, so the five new en/es pairs live in the catalogs where the parity test can see them. ticket-start.mjs stays a thin caller: it prints and exits before any git work, so a refusal creates no branch and no worktree.
